kpis.name: URLs offered in the sitemap
kpis.why: Not a score to maximise. It was 312, of which 216 were client-by-product setup permutations measuring 73.6-77.5% similar to each other; Googlebot read the sitemap 7 times and then crawled 2 pages. Cut to 96 on 2026-09-07 and the permutations marked noindex,follow. See docs/SEO_INDEXATION_R1.md.

kpis.name: Google impressions, storefront
kpis.how: data/gsc.json, Search Console sc-domain:zovo.one filtered to //mcp.zovo.one/ pages, with a positive control on //zovo.one/ returning 63 clicks and 4,392 impressions to prove the filter works
kpis.why: Zero here across 99+ days means Google has never shown this site to anyone. It is the single most important organic number.

kpis.name: Googlebot URL coverage
kpis.how: data/traffic.json crawler_url_coverage, Cloudflare GraphQL by user agent
kpis.why: Googlebot fetched robots.txt 4x and sitemap.xml 7x in the same window and then crawled 2 pages. It is declining, not blocked.

kpis.name: ClaudeBot URL coverage
kpis.why: Assistant crawlers have this catalogue even though Google does not. This is the discovery channel that is actually working.

kpis.name: Human page views, storefront
kpis.how: data/traffic.json human_evidence, browser user agents confirmed by a render-engine test (did that exact UA ever fetch favicon, cdn-cgi or assets); 33 of 124 browser-shaped UA strings passed
kpis.why: The honest size of the audience. A spoofed UA that never loads an asset is not a person.

kpis.name: GitHub unique visitors
kpis.why: The repo is the other front door. 0 stars, 0 forks and 0 watchers since 2026-09-02.

kpis.name: Release asset fetches (mostly automated)
kpis.how: gh api releases (scripts/measure.mjs). NOT an install count: across 597 assets the counts are near-uniform (mean 8.90, median 8, p10 6, p90 11, top 10 of 597 hold 5.7%), and obsolete releases score the same per asset as the current one. Human demand is a power law; this is machine sweeping. See docs/AUDIENCE_REALITY_R1.md.
kpis.why: Kept for continuity only. It was previously reported as an install metric against a target of 1,000 and read as met, which was wrong.

kpis.why: One key per paid session; zero means no purchase reached /success.

kpis.name: Upgrade link clicks (humans, 7d)
kpis.how: GET https://mcp.zovo.one/stats/clicks, sum of by_src[*].last7d. WARNING: the worker guard is start-anchored, so any browser User-Agent is counted, including this project's own agents. docs/CONVERSION_R1.md measured 77.9% of clicks carrying a src no live page emits. Treat as an upper bound, never as human demand.
kpis.why: The click is the step between a cap message and a checkout session; without it a stalled funnel and a message nobody reads look the same.

kpis.name: Click to checkout-session ratio
kpis.how: 100 * checkout sessions from humans (last 100, Stripe) / upgrade link clicks (7d, /stats/clicks) - the two windows differ (last 100 ever vs last 7 days), so this is an approximation, not the true window-matched ratio
kpis.why: Separates whether people are seeing the link (clicks) from whether the checkout page itself converts (ratio); a link with clicks and no sessions points at the redirect or the Stripe page, not the message.

kpis.name: Pro tenants on hosted endpoints
kpis.how: Stripe-bound tenants (REMOTE_DATA bind: prefix, 0) plus distinct lic: tenant ids whose key the billing worker minted (LICENSES session:*, 0 keys). EXCLUDED: the 2625 raw lic: documents are per (key, server) pairs, not tenants (248 distinct ids), and 248 of those ids are validation probes signed locally by scripts/sign-license.mjs, never bought.
kpis.why: Real Pro usage on hosted. The old count read every lic: document, so one validation run over 16 servers looked like 16 paying tenants.

stripe.note: sessions created before 2026-09-03 08:55 UTC predate probe tagging and are excluded
